case_name: Syed Yousuf Hussain v State of Andhra Pradesh
respondent:
State of Andhra Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

5 April 2013
Cr.A. No. 539 of 2013 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) No. 6354 of 2012)
The Judgment was delivered by : Dipak Misra, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. The present Appeal by Special Leave is directed against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 29.12.2012 in Criminal Appeal No. 466 of 2005 passed by the High Court of Judicature of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad whereby the Division Bench, while maintaining the conviction for the offences punishable u/ss. 7 and 13(1)(d) read with S. 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (for brevity "the Act") read with Section 34, I.P.C. since the accused-appellant was convicted along with another accused, namely, Mohd. Shafi-Ul-Haq, recorded by the Principal Special Judge for S.P.E. and A.C.B. Cases-cum-IV Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad, in C.C. No. 11 of 1995, reduced the sentence to that of simple imprisonment for six months for the off
facts: On 4.1.1994, PW-2, Mohd. Shareef, a driver in the Cuddapah Transport Company, Hyderabad was driving a lorry bearing No. AP 04-T-372 in Hyderabad near Tadbund and was proceeding towards Musheerabad locality via Santoshnagar cross-road.
The accused-appellant (hereinafter referred to as 'the accused') along with the other accused stopped the vehicle on the pretext that the lorry had entered the 'No Entry Zone'.

PW-2, who was asked to pay the amount by the evening, did not have any intention to give the bribe and, accordingly, approached the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Hyderabad, PW-6, and lodged a complaint.
The trap party along with others and PW-2 reached Kamal Talkies about 7.00 P.M. where PW-2 met the accused persons at Chadarghat Junction.
Accused No. 2 accepted the bribe amount of Rs.100/- in the presence of the present appellant and returned the documents.
issues: Whether the prosecution has proved the acceptance of the amount by the accused No. 2?
Whether the accused-appellant was involved in the commission of the offence?
petitioner_arguments: The evidence brought on record by the prosecution is absolutely sketchy and do not even hazily point out towards the involvement of the accused.
He had abetted in the commission of the crime and definitely had the intention to demand and accept the bribe.
respondent_arguments: The learned trial Judge as well as the High Court has scrutinized the evidence in detail and correctly reached the conclusion that the demand and acceptance was done with his consent.
Both the accused persons were on duty at the relevant place at the relevant time and the vehicle was intercepted and the documents were taken away by the accused.
court_reasoning: The trial court has referred to Ext. P-12, the order book of the Traffic Police Station, Yakutpura.

Appreciating the cumulative effect of the aforesaid evidence, the trial Judge had come to the conclusion that both the accused persons were on duty at the relevant place at the relevant time and the vehicle was intercepted and the documents were taken away by the accused.
holding: The conviction and reduced sentence as mentioned earlier are sustained.
